claims.summary: For A_a=[[a,sqrt(1+a),0],[sqrt(1+a),0,0],[0,0,1]], 0<a<=1/3, spectrum {1+a,-1,1}, and iid Uniform[0,1] inputs, the scalar-square absolute half-Riesz interface H(a)=a^{-1/2} E|X_2^2-((1+a)/a)X_1^2|^{-1/2} is at least (1/sqrt(1+a))*log(sqrt((1+a)/a)/2), hence diverges logarithmically as a downarrow 0, while the actual output density is uniformly bounded by the prior fixed-principal-triple theorem. This refutes that proof interface, not QFORM.

In the exact rank-three physical coloop geometry, every fixed nonzero pivot a obeys ||p_Q||_infinity <=16*sqrt(30)(|a||det Lambda|)^(-1/4) by the zero-affine specialization of the completed rank-two half-Riesz theorem. The qualitative nonzero-pivot scope was already implicit in that source; this records the sharper specialization and exposes the near-zero logarithmic interface loss.

The run independently rederived an n=3 bound via scalar-pivot/indefinite-pair dichotomy, but a prior complete theorem QFORM-FIXED-MATRIX-BOUNDED-v1 already gives the stronger ||p_Q||_infinity <=2*pi+3*sqrt(3) when n=3 and sigma_min(A)>=1. No novelty claim is retained.
